# Initiative Brief: init-salescoach-mvp

## Problem

Sales representatives consistently enter high-stakes calls underprepared — without a structured plan, without awareness of which discovery questions to prioritize, and without real-time support when conversations drift off track. Post-call feedback arrives too late and too subjectively to drive behavior change. Industry data shows reps forget 70% of training within a week, and fewer than 40% of calls follow any structured methodology (SPICED, MEDDPICC, etc.). Existing tools (Gong, Chorus, Clari) focus on post-call analytics and manager visibility — none provide decision support in the moment when it matters most.

## Goals

- Deliver an AI-driven pre-call planning system that reaches Minimum Viable Clarity (MVC) through LLM-powered conversational intake, replacing static checklists with adaptive questioning
- Provide real-time coaching cues during live calls — sparse, contextual, and non-intrusive (max 1 cue per 30-45 seconds) — surfaced at the exact moment they are useful
- Generate structured post-call deliverables: summary, scorecard (8 categories), one strength, one improvement area, and one concrete practice recommendation
- Support guidebook-driven coaching flows using SPICED (primary) and MEDDPICC (secondary) sales frameworks, with architecture ready for additional frameworks post-MVP
- Achieve sub-500ms latency for both coaching cue delivery and transcription display during live calls
- Prove the end-to-end loop — Prepare, Call, Coach, Review, Improve — in a single-user web application

## Non-Goals

- We are NOT building CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, GoHighLevel) in this phase
- No multi-user roles, manager dashboards, team reporting, or rep ranking — this is a single-rep private tool
- No mobile app — desktop browser only (Chrome primary, Firefox/Edge secondary)
- No PSTN/SIP telephony integration — audio captured from rep's local device
- No multi-language coaching — English only
- No emotion recognition, sentiment scoring, or engagement detection during calls
- No compliance enforcement engine or legal/procurement advice
- No persistent learning across users or longitudinal rep skill profiles (architecturally supported, deferred)
- No real-time scoring, probability boards, or advanced analytics during calls
- We will NOT build the full framework elimination decision tree — a placeholder (SPICED + MEDDPICC) is used for MVP, replaceable post-launch without interface changes

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pre-call conversational intake completes Q1-Q3 super-clarifying questions with LLM-driven data extraction and contextual follow-ups until all required fields are filled
- Framework selection returns SPICED (primary) + MEDDPICC (secondary) and proceeds to guidebook-derived question packs for missing fields
- Call Reasoning (CR1-CR5), Persona (P1-P5), and Demographics (D1-D5) stages complete sequentially, each gated by a fire-once completion event
- Call plan is generated with: objective, 3 priorities, 2 risks, target next step, and unknowns list
- Live transcription displays with speaker diarization (rep vs. prospect) at sub-500ms latency via AssemblyAI streaming
- Coaching cues appear on-screen within 500ms of trigger detection, throttled to max 1 per 30 seconds
- Post-call summary, scorecard, and lessons are generated within 10 seconds of call end
- All extracted data carries confidence tags (confirmed, inferred, assumed)
- WebSocket reconnects automatically (max 5 attempts, 3s delay) without losing call state
- LLM provider failover switches between Cerebras and OpenAI transparently on provider failure
- UI renders with OnPush change detection — no visible jank during live call with concurrent transcript + coaching cue updates
- All event-driven communication flows through EventBus — no direct handler-to-handler calls

## Stakeholders

- **Product Owner & Technical Lead:** Sole founder-developer — owns product vision, architecture, and all implementation
- **Target User Persona:** Sales Representative (Individual Contributor) — runs their own calls, uses SalesCoach privately, wants to improve outcomes and consistency without manager oversight
- **LLM Providers:** Cerebras (primary, fast inference) and OpenAI (fallback, broad model support)
- **STT Provider:** AssemblyAI (v3 streaming API with turn-level formatting)
- **TTS Providers:** ElevenLabs and FishAudio via Voice Engine proxy
- **Design System:** Fuse Admin Template + Angular Material + TailwindCSS (Royal Blue #1D7AE6, Teal #0D7F86, Emerald #22C6B8)

## Timeline

- **Phase 0 — Foundation & Infrastructure:** COMPLETE
- **Phase 1 — PCRC Q1-Q3 LLM-Driven Questions:** COMPLETE
- **Phase 2 — Framework Selection + Guidebook Questions:** 5.5 days (placeholder selection + question packs for missing fields)
- **Phase 3 — Call Reasoning + Persona + Demographics:** 4-5 days (CR1-CR5, P1-P5, D1-D5 sequential stages)
- **Phase 4 — Enhanced Call Plan Generation:** 3-4 days (objective, priorities, risks, next step, unknowns)
- **Phase 5 — Live Coaching AI:** 5-7 days (trigger detection, cue generation, throttling, degraded mode)
- **Phase 6 — Post-Call AI:** 4-5 days (summary generation, 8-category scoring, lessons learned)
- **Phase 7 — End-to-End Testing & Performance Validation:** 5-7 days (full journey testing, latency validation, WebSocket resilience)
- **Target MVP Complete:** ~4-5 weeks from current state

## Budget

- Engineering: 1 founder-developer, full-time (~5 weeks remaining to MVP)
- Infrastructure (monthly):
  - Cerebras API: ~$50-150/month (primary LLM inference)
  - OpenAI API: ~$30-80/month (fallback LLM)
  - AssemblyAI: ~$50-100/month (streaming STT)
  - ElevenLabs/FishAudio: ~$20-50/month (TTS)
  - AWS ECS + MongoDB: ~$150-300/month (compute, database, ALB)
- Total estimated monthly run cost: ~$300-680/month

## Constraints

- Single developer — all frontend, backend, AI integration, infrastructure, and testing done by one person; scope must remain tightly controlled
- Must use existing tech stack: Angular 19 + Node.js/Express + MongoDB + WebSocket — no new frameworks or databases
- All backend handler communication must flow through the EventBus pub/sub system — no direct handler-to-handler calls permitted
- PCRC-LLM Handler is the sole orchestrator for all pre-call stages — old individual handlers (CallReasoning, Persona, Demographics) remain disabled to prevent conflicts
- LLM model names must never be hardcoded — providers use environment-configured defaults (`CEREBRAS_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL`)
- Coaching cues must be non-intrusive: max 1 per 30-45 seconds, suppressible when transcription confidence drops
- Audio processing must use Opus/Ogg for streaming (not MP3) — `ogg-opus-decoder` for browser, not `opus-stream-decoder` which has Node.js dependencies
- All stage completion events must fire exactly once per callId (enforced via `Set<string>` guards)
- Frontend uses OnPush change detection — all async state changes require explicit `markForCheck()`

## Dependencies

- **AssemblyAI v3 Streaming API** — real-time transcription with `format_turns=true` and `ForceEndpoint` message support
- **Cerebras API** — primary LLM provider for fast inference (sub-second response for extraction and coaching)
- **OpenAI API** — fallback LLM provider when Cerebras is unavailable or degraded
- **Voice Engine Proxy** (prototypedemos.com) — proxies TTS requests to ElevenLabs/FishAudio
- **MongoDB** — persistent storage for users, campaigns, contacts, call sessions, transcripts, and call plans
- **SPICED + MEDDPICC Guidebook Data** — loaded from JSON into GuidebookStore at startup; defines dimensions, required fields, and question banks
- **Pre-Call Questions Schema** (`precall-questions-schema.json`) — defines initial questions, field metadata, and extraction rules for Q1-Q3
- **Fuse Admin Template** — Angular Material + TailwindCSS design system providing layout, navigation, and component library
- **Docker + Nginx** — containerized deployment with reverse proxy for WebSocket upgrade support
- **AWS ECS** — production hosting (ECR for images, Secrets Manager for API keys, ALB for traffic)

# Initiative Brief: init-salescoach-mvp

## Problem

Sales representatives consistently enter high-stakes calls underprepared — without a structured plan, without awareness of which discovery questions to prioritize, and without real-time support when conversations drift off track. Post-call feedback arrives too late and too subjectively to drive behavior change. Industry data shows reps forget 70% of training within a week, and fewer than 40% of calls follow any structured methodology (SPICED, MEDDPICC, etc.). Existing tools (Gong, Chorus, Clari) focus on post-call analytics and manager visibility — none provide decision support in the moment when it matters most.

## Goals

- Deliver an AI-driven pre-call planning system that reaches Minimum Viable Clarity (MVC) through LLM-powered conversational intake, replacing static checklists with adaptive questioning
- Provide real-time coaching cues during live calls — sparse, contextual, and non-intrusive (max 1 cue per 30-45 seconds) — surfaced at the exact moment they are useful
- Generate structured post-call deliverables: summary, scorecard (8 categories), one strength, one improvement area, and one concrete practice recommendation
- Support guidebook-driven coaching flows using SPICED (primary) and MEDDPICC (secondary) sales frameworks, with architecture ready for additional frameworks post-MVP
- Achieve sub-500ms latency for both coaching cue delivery and transcription display during live calls
- Prove the end-to-end loop — Prepare, Call, Coach, Review, Improve — in a single-user web application

## Non-Goals

- We are NOT building CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, GoHighLevel) in this phase
- No multi-user roles, manager dashboards, team reporting, or rep ranking — this is a single-rep private tool
- No mobile app — desktop browser only (Chrome primary, Firefox/Edge secondary)
- No PSTN/SIP telephony integration — audio captured from rep's local device
- No multi-language coaching — English only
- No emotion recognition, sentiment scoring, or engagement detection during calls
- No compliance enforcement engine or legal/procurement advice
- No persistent learning across users or longitudinal rep skill profiles (architecturally supported, deferred)
- No real-time scoring, probability boards, or advanced analytics during calls
- We will NOT build the full framework elimination decision tree — a placeholder (SPICED + MEDDPICC) is used for MVP, replaceable post-launch without interface changes

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pre-call conversational intake completes Q1-Q3 super-clarifying questions with LLM-driven data extraction and contextual follow-ups until all required fields are filled
- Framework selection returns SPICED (primary) + MEDDPICC (secondary) and proceeds to guidebook-derived question packs for missing fields
- Call Reasoning (CR1-CR5), Persona (P1-P5), and Demographics (D1-D5) stages complete sequentially, each gated by a fire-once completion event
- Call plan is generated with: objective, 3 priorities, 2 risks, target next step, and unknowns list
- Live transcription displays with speaker diarization (rep vs. prospect) at sub-500ms latency via AssemblyAI streaming
- Coaching cues appear on-screen within 500ms of trigger detection, throttled to max 1 per 30 seconds
- Post-call summary, scorecard, and lessons are generated within 10 seconds of call end
- All extracted data carries confidence tags (confirmed, inferred, assumed)
- WebSocket reconnects automatically (max 5 attempts, 3s delay) without losing call state
- LLM provider failover switches between Cerebras and OpenAI transparently on provider failure
- UI renders with OnPush change detection — no visible jank during live call with concurrent transcript + coaching cue updates
- All event-driven communication flows through EventBus — no direct handler-to-handler calls

## Stakeholders

- **Product Owner & Technical Lead:** Sole founder-developer — owns product vision, architecture, and all implementation
- **Target User Persona:** Sales Representative (Individual Contributor) — runs their own calls, uses SalesCoach privately, wants to improve outcomes and consistency without manager oversight
- **LLM Providers:** Cerebras (primary, fast inference) and OpenAI (fallback, broad model support)
- **STT Provider:** AssemblyAI (v3 streaming API with turn-level formatting)
- **TTS Providers:** ElevenLabs and FishAudio via Voice Engine proxy
- **Design System:** Fuse Admin Template + Angular Material + TailwindCSS (Royal Blue #1D7AE6, Teal #0D7F86, Emerald #22C6B8)

## Timeline

- **Phase 0 — Foundation & Infrastructure:** COMPLETE
- **Phase 1 — PCRC Q1-Q3 LLM-Driven Questions:** COMPLETE
- **Phase 2 — Framework Selection + Guidebook Questions:** 5.5 days (placeholder selection + question packs for missing fields)
- **Phase 3 — Call Reasoning + Persona + Demographics:** 4-5 days (CR1-CR5, P1-P5, D1-D5 sequential stages)
- **Phase 4 — Enhanced Call Plan Generation:** 3-4 days (objective, priorities, risks, next step, unknowns)
- **Phase 5 — Live Coaching AI:** 5-7 days (trigger detection, cue generation, throttling, degraded mode)
- **Phase 6 — Post-Call AI:** 4-5 days (summary generation, 8-category scoring, lessons learned)
- **Phase 7 — End-to-End Testing & Performance Validation:** 5-7 days (full journey testing, latency validation, WebSocket resilience)
- **Target MVP Complete:** ~4-5 weeks from current state

## Budget

- Engineering: 1 founder-developer, full-time (~5 weeks remaining to MVP)
- Infrastructure (monthly):
  - Cerebras API: ~$50-150/month (primary LLM inference)
  - OpenAI API: ~$30-80/month (fallback LLM)
  - AssemblyAI: ~$50-100/month (streaming STT)
  - ElevenLabs/FishAudio: ~$20-50/month (TTS)
  - AWS ECS + MongoDB: ~$150-300/month (compute, database, ALB)
- Total estimated monthly run cost: ~$300-680/month

## Constraints

- Single developer — all frontend, backend, AI integration, infrastructure, and testing done by one person; scope must remain tightly controlled
- Must use existing tech stack: Angular 19 + Node.js/Express + MongoDB + WebSocket — no new frameworks or databases
- All backend handler communication must flow through the EventBus pub/sub system — no direct handler-to-handler calls permitted
- PCRC-LLM Handler is the sole orchestrator for all pre-call stages — old individual handlers (CallReasoning, Persona, Demographics) remain disabled to prevent conflicts
- LLM model names must never be hardcoded — providers use environment-configured defaults (`CEREBRAS_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL`)
- Coaching cues must be non-intrusive: max 1 per 30-45 seconds, suppressible when transcription confidence drops
- Audio processing must use Opus/Ogg for streaming (not MP3) — `ogg-opus-decoder` for browser, not `opus-stream-decoder` which has Node.js dependencies
- All stage completion events must fire exactly once per callId (enforced via `Set<string>` guards)
- Frontend uses OnPush change detection — all async state changes require explicit `markForCheck()`

## Dependencies

- **AssemblyAI v3 Streaming API** — real-time transcription with `format_turns=true` and `ForceEndpoint` message support
- **Cerebras API** — primary LLM provider for fast inference (sub-second response for extraction and coaching)
- **OpenAI API** — fallback LLM provider when Cerebras is unavailable or degraded
- **Voice Engine Proxy** (prototypedemos.com) — proxies TTS requests to ElevenLabs/FishAudio
- **MongoDB** — persistent storage for users, campaigns, contacts, call sessions, transcripts, and call plans
- **SPICED + MEDDPICC Guidebook Data** — loaded from JSON into GuidebookStore at startup; defines dimensions, required fields, and question banks
- **Pre-Call Questions Schema** (`precall-questions-schema.json`) — defines initial questions, field metadata, and extraction rules for Q1-Q3
- **Fuse Admin Template** — Angular Material + TailwindCSS design system providing layout, navigation, and component library
- **Docker + Nginx** — containerized deployment with reverse proxy for WebSocket upgrade support
- **AWS ECS** — production hosting (ECR for images, Secrets Manager for API keys, ALB for traffic)

# Initiative Brief: init-salescoach-mvp

## Problem

Sales representatives consistently enter high-stakes calls underprepared — without a structured plan, without awareness of which discovery questions to prioritize, and without real-time support when conversations drift off track. Post-call feedback arrives too late and too subjectively to drive behavior change. Industry data shows reps forget 70% of training within a week, and fewer than 40% of calls follow any structured methodology (SPICED, MEDDPICC, etc.). Existing tools (Gong, Chorus, Clari) focus on post-call analytics and manager visibility — none provide decision support in the moment when it matters most.

## Goals

- Deliver an AI-driven pre-call planning system that reaches Minimum Viable Clarity (MVC) through LLM-powered conversational intake, replacing static checklists with adaptive questioning
- Provide real-time coaching cues during live calls — sparse, contextual, and non-intrusive (max 1 cue per 30-45 seconds) — surfaced at the exact moment they are useful
- Generate structured post-call deliverables: summary, scorecard (8 categories), one strength, one improvement area, and one concrete practice recommendation
- Support guidebook-driven coaching flows using SPICED (primary) and MEDDPICC (secondary) sales frameworks, with architecture ready for additional frameworks post-MVP
- Achieve sub-500ms latency for both coaching cue delivery and transcription display during live calls

- We are NOT building CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, GoHighLevel) in this phase
- No multi-user roles, manager dashboards, team reporting, or rep ranking — this is a single-rep private tool
- No mobile app — desktop browser only (Chrome primary, Firefox/Edge secondary)
- No PSTN/SIP telephony integration — audio captured from rep's local device
- No multi-language coaching — English only
- No emotion recognition, sentiment scoring, or engagement detection during calls

- No real-time scoring, probability boards, or advanced analytics during calls

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC-01** [P1]: Pre-call conversational intake completes Q1-Q3 super-clarifying questions with LLM-driven data extraction and contextual follow-ups until all required fields are filled
- **AC-02** [P1]: Framework selection returns SPICED (primary) + MEDDPICC (secondary) and proceeds to guidebook-derived question packs for missing fields
- **AC-03** [P1]: Call Reasoning (CR1-CR5), Persona (P1-P5), and Demographics (D1-D5) stages complete sequentially, each gated by a fire-once completion event
- **AC-04** [P1]: Call plan is generated with: objective, 3 priorities, 2 risks, target next step, and unknowns list
- **AC-05** [P1]: Live transcription displays with speaker diarization (rep vs. prospect) at sub-500ms latency via AssemblyAI streaming
- **AC-06** [P1]: Coaching cues appear on-screen within 500ms of trigger detection, throttled to max 1 per 30 seconds
- **AC-07** [P1]: Post-call summary, scorecard, and lessons are generated within 10 seconds of call end
- **AC-08** [P1]: All extracted data carries confidence tags (confirmed, inferred, assumed)
- **AC-09** [P1]: WebSocket reconnects automatically (max 5 attempts, 3s delay) without losing call state
- **AC-10** [P1]: LLM provider failover switches between Cerebras and OpenAI transparently on provider failure
- **AC-11** [P1]: UI renders with OnPush change detection — no visible jank during live call with concurrent transcript + coaching cue updates
- **AC-12** [P1]: All event-driven communication flows through EventBus — no direct handler-to-handler calls

## Constraints
- Single developer — all frontend, backend, AI integration, infrastructure, and testing done by one person; scope must remain tightly controlled
- Must use existing tech stack: Angular 19 + Node.js/Express + MongoDB + WebSocket — no new frameworks or databases
- All backend handler communication must flow through the EventBus pub/sub system — no direct handler-to-handler calls permitted
- PCRC-LLM Handler is the sole orchestrator for all pre-call stages — old individual handlers (CallReasoning, Persona, Demographics) remain disabled to prevent conflicts
- LLM model names must never be hardcoded — providers use environment-configured defaults (`CEREBRAS_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL`)
- Coaching cues must be non-intrusive: max 1 per 30-45 seconds, suppressible when transcription confidence drops
- Audio processing must use Opus/Ogg for streaming (not MP3) — `ogg-opus-decoder` for browser, not `opus-stream-decoder` which has Node.js dependencies
- All stage completion events must fire exactly once per callId (enforced via `Set<string>` guards)
- Frontend uses OnPush change detection — all async state changes require explicit `markForCheck()`

On reconnect (max 5 attempts, 3s delay), backend MUST rehydrate call state from websocketCallStateSnapshot in MongoDB keyed by callId. Transcript and cue updates must be emitted so UI can meet sub-500ms transcript display and <=500ms cue display targets.
- **EventBus: backend internal pub/sub** (event): Sole internal communication mechanism; disallows direct handler-to-handler calls.
  Contract: AC-12: All event-driven communication flows through EventBus; no direct handler-to-handler calls permitted. Stage completion, transcriptTurn publish, coachingCue publish, and post-call generation triggers MUST be communicated via EventBus.
- **AssemblyAI v3 Streaming adapter** (api): Adapter for AssemblyAI v3 streaming diarized turns and event mapping to transcriptTurn.
  Contract: AC-05/AC-12: Use AssemblyAI v3 streaming with format_turns=true and ForceEndpoint support. Adapter MUST emit diarized transcriptTurn events (speaker rep vs prospect) and include adapter timing metadata to validate sub-500ms UI display budget.
- **LLM Provider Router (Cerebras primary -> OpenAI fallback)** (shared-lib): Unified structured-output router with transparent failover between Cerebras and OpenAI.
  Contract: AC-10: On provider failure/degradation, transparently switch Cerebras -> OpenAI while preserving unified structured output schema used by extraction, cue triggering, call plan generation, and post-call generation. Constraint: model names are environment-configured only.
- **PCRC-LLM Handler orchestrator** (shared-lib): Sole orchestrator for pre-call stages, sequential stage execution, and generation flows.

- **GuidebookStore (SPICED+MEDDPICC loader)** (shared-lib): Loads guidebook JSON into an in-memory store at startup; serves question packs for missing fields.

- **PrecallQuestionSchema loader** (shared-lib): Loads precall-questions-schema.json defining Q1-Q3, required fields, and extraction rules.

- **MongoDB CallState repository** (database): Persists call sessions, stage completion markers, call plans, post-call deliverables, and reconnect snapshots.

- **Cue Policy Service** (shared-lib): Server-side enforcement for coaching cue non-intrusiveness (throttling) and suppression behavior.

### Architecture Decision Records
- **ADR-001: EventBus-only internal communication (AC-12)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-12: All event-driven communication flows through EventBus — no direct handler-to-handler calls. Constraint: All backend handler communication must flow through EventBus pub/sub.
  Decision: Implement backend modules so they communicate exclusively through EventBus pub/sub. Disallow direct handler-to-handler calls via code review policy and automated checks where possible.
- **ADR-002: PCRC-LLM Handler sole orchestrator with exact-once stage completion guards (AC-03)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-03: CR1-CR5, P1-P5, D1-D5 stages complete sequentially with fire-once completion event. Constraint: PCRC-LLM Handler is sole orchestrator; old handlers disabled. Constraint: stage completion events must fire exactly once per callId enforced via Set<string> guards.
  Decision: Centralize stage flow in PCRC-LLM Handler. Maintain per-call Set<string> for emitted stageIds and only publish StageCompletionEvent once per callId+stageId. Enforce sequential progression in orchestration logic.
- **ADR-003: Confidence-tagged extraction loop until schema-required fields are complete (AC-01, AC-08)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-01: Q1-Q3 intake continues with LLM-driven extraction and follow-ups until required fields filled. AC-08: extracted data carries confidence tags. Dependency: precall-questions-schema.json defines required fields and extraction rules.
  Decision: Use precall-questions-schema.json to define required fields. Produce ExtractedFieldValue outputs with confidenceTag for every extracted field. Continue interaction until requiredFieldsStatus indicates all required fields are complete.
- **ADR-004: Transparent LLM failover via Provider Router preserving unified structured outputs (AC-10)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-10: failover switches between Cerebras and OpenAI transparently on provider failure. Constraint: model names not hardcoded; use env defaults.
  Decision: Implement LLM Provider Router used by PCRC-LLM Handler. Attempt Cerebras first; on failure/degradation fall back to OpenAI while keeping identical structured output schema for downstream processing.
- **ADR-005: Sub-500ms diarized transcript updates using AssemblyAI streaming hot path (AC-05)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-05: speaker diarization at sub-500ms latency via AssemblyAI streaming.
  Decision: Enable AssemblyAI v3 streaming with format_turns=true and ForceEndpoint support. Convert events directly into transcriptTurn and attach adapterPublishedAtMs for measurable latency enforcement.
- **ADR-006: Server-side coaching cue policy: <=500ms render, throttling, and suppression (AC-06)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-06: cues appear within 500ms of trigger detection; throttled to max 1 per 30 seconds; suppressible when transcription confidence drops.
  Decision: Cue policy service enforces throttling <=1 per 30 seconds and suppression based on transcription confidence. Cues include uiDeadlineMs to support meeting the 500ms render deadline.
- **ADR-007: WebSocket reconnect state restoration without losing call state (AC-09)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-09: reconnects automatically (max 5 attempts, 3s delay) without losing call state.
  Decision: Persist websocketCallStateSnapshot keyed by callId containing currentStage, completedStageIds, and lastTranscriptTurnSequence/lastCueSequence. On reconnect, rehydrate state from snapshot and resume streaming using sequence markers so history is not lost.
- **ADR-008: Post-call deliverables generation within 10 seconds of call end (AC-07)** [accepted]
  Context: AC-07: post-call summary, scorecard, lessons generated within 10 seconds of call end.
  Decision: Trigger postCallDeliverables generation on call-end event and enforce a strict timing budget to produce the required structured deliverables in the specified schema within 10 seconds.

### Security Baseline
- Auth: Assumed TBD: Contract does not specify auth. For operational readiness, implement at least a single-user session gate to prevent unauthorized access to WebSocket call streams and callId snapshot data (assumption, required for AC-09 leakage risk).
- Data classification: Assumed sensitive: live transcripts (diarized), extracted confidence-tagged fields, coaching cues, call plans, and post-call deliverables.
- Threats: Unauthorized WebSocket access leaking transcriptTurn/coachingCue content (AC-09)., Call state bleed/cross-call leakage via incorrect callId scoping and snapshot retrieval (AC-09)., Duplicate/incorrect stage completion due to repeated triggers without exact-once enforcement (AC-03)., Prompt injection via transcript content altering extraction/cue outputs (AC-01/AC-06)., Malformed structured outputs during LLM failover breaking cue/plan/post-call generation (AC-10).

### Scalability
- Expected load: Single-user private tool. Live call: frequent transcriptTurn updates; coaching cues throttled to max 1 per 30 seconds (AC-06). Pre-call and post-call include LLM-driven extraction/generation operations (AC-01/AC-07).
- Bottlenecks: AssemblyAI->WebSocket->UI timing for transcript display (AC-05)., Trigger detection->Cue policy->WebSocket->UI timing for cues (AC-06)., UI render stability under concurrent transcript and cue updates (AC-11)., Reconnect rehydration time for state restoration (AC-09)., Provider failover tail latency and schema consistency (AC-10).

### Architect Flagged Gaps
- Auth method is not specified in the contract; securityBaseline.authMethod is assumed TBD for readiness verification (AC-09 leakage risk).
- The contract does not specify the exact field name/type for transcription confidence used for cue suppression; implementation must map AssemblyAI confidence to cue suppression rule while maintaining AC-06.
